title: PageBackdropManifest
description: The wire contract between the producer — design-parity's Figma page importer — and any consumer that draws the result: a preview server, an IDE panel, or the bundled offline HTML viewer. The producer emits a design page's geometry and its design→code mapping; how it is drawn is entirely the consumer's decision. Prose spec: docs/page-backdrop-contract.md.

version.description: Equals PAGE_BACKDROP_VERSION. Bumped only for a BREAKING shape change; additive optional fields never bump it. A consumer should accept any version it understands rather than requiring equality, because the producer releases independently of every consumer.

source.description: The design source the pages came from. Only Figma exposes a page-level read API today.

fileKey.description: Design-tool file the pages were imported from.

pages.description: Imported pages, in the order the committed config listed them — the repo's own stated priority.

PageRect.description: An axis-aligned rectangle in the page's frame-local design units (dp), origin at the frame's top-left. Deliberately NOT image pixels: the backdrop PNG is exported at some scale, and pinning geometry to the unscaled frame means a re-export at a different resolution does not invalidate the manifest. Consumers position by ratio (x / frame.width), so no density arithmetic is needed anywhere.

PlacementLink.description: How a placement was linked to code. 'code-connect' is Figma's machine link; 'manifest' is the repo's design-map.json; 'convention' is a best-effort name match; 'unlinked' means nothing matched — which is a finding, not an omission.

Placement.description: One component instance found on the page, and the code it maps to. An instance nothing matched is still a placement: 'this part of the screen has no code behind it' is exactly what a whole-screen view exists to surface.

nodeId.description: Node id of the instance on the page.

componentId.description: Node id of the instance's main component, when the source reports one. This — not nodeId — is what Code Connect links against.

componentSetId.description: Node id of the main component's set, when the component is one variant of a set. Code Connect commonly links the set rather than a single variant, so it is tried first.

depth.description: Nesting depth below the page frame; 0 for a top-level instance. Greater than 0 only when the import ran with nested: true.

ref.description: The instance's own design ref, "figma:<fileKey>/<nodeId>". Always present, linked or not, so a consumer can deep-link a hotspot back into the design tool even for a part of the screen no code implements.

code.description: Code handle, e.g. "ui/Button.kt#PrimaryButton". Absent when unlinked.

previewId.description: Fully-qualified preview id of the code component, when design-map.json names one. Present so a consumer can render the component itself — a preview server keys on previewId, and without this it would need the producer's own inputs to turn a code handle into something renderable.

confidence.description: How much to trust `code`. Stated rather than implied by `link`, so a consumer need not hardcode which methods are weak. code-connect and manifest are high; convention is always low. Absent when unlinked.

matchedRef.description: The design ref the link actually matched on, so a reader can tell whether the component set, the main component, or the instance carried the link.

uri.description: Path to the image, relative to the manifest file.

scale.description: Export scale the PNG was rendered at; 2 means the PNG is 2x `frame`. Carried but meaningless for an SVG, which has no raster size.

format.description: How the backdrop was exported. Absent means `png` — the only format version 1 originally had, so an older committed manifest reads correctly unchanged. `svg` means the file carries `data-node-id` on every element, i.e. a consumer can find the element for any placement's `nodeId` rather than only knowing where it sits.

id.description: Stable slug, unique within the manifest; also the backdrop PNG's basename.

name.description: The frame's layer name in the design file.

nodeId.description: Node id of the page frame.

frame.description: The frame's size in design units — the coordinate space every placement's bounds live in.

placements.description: Component instances on the page, ordered top-left first so a re-import diffs cleanly.
